notes.note: Genesis 8:1 is retained as a narrative water/wind parallel. It is not a claim that the source words for wind and Spirit have been independently collated or that the two scenes are identical.
John 1:4-5 is a theological light/darkness analogy. It is not labelled a quotation of this individual verse.
Same-chapter evening/morning refrains are literary cross-references. Each source/target direction is a distinct pair; no inference of historical dependence between adjacent verses is intended.
Firmament and upper-water language is retained from the supplied edition without a new cosmological or scientific interpretation.
Genesis 8:17 repeats multiplication language at the creatures' release, while the command in the supplied English reading addresses Noah.

Connections with Sirach, Wisdom, Psalms and James concern image, human dignity and responsibility toward creatures. No independent original-language collation or specialist doctrinal adjudication is claimed.
The supplied Greek-based Genesis 2:2 says God completed His work on the sixth day. That source wording is preserved; it is not silently replaced by a different edition's seventh-day reading.
The supplied Genesis says completion on the sixth day and rest on the seventh. Hebrews quotes the rest clause. The supplied sixth-day completion reading remains intact.

The supplied Job says divine spirit made the speaker and the Almighty's breath teaches him. The retained comparison concerns divine agency and clay; it does not replace the teaching statement with another edition's life-giving-breath wording. This distinction was corrected during peer QA.
The named-river comparison uses actual Sirach units 25-27, with no missing 24:24 unit inserted. No modern location or reconstruction of Eden's river courses is asserted.

Later marriage and formation texts are linked to the actual creation passages. The comparison does not claim that all later statements on authority, childbearing, Christ or the Church occur explicitly in Genesis.
The woman says nor shall you touch it in this supplied text. The earlier command at Genesis 2:17 is quoted exactly; no new conclusion about an omitted divine command or textual error is imposed.

The supplied Greek-based wording is He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel. Romans 16:20 and Luke 10:19 are labelled later Christian thematic associations, not quotations or a claim that Genesis itself uses the word crush or explicitly names Satan.
The link records shared references to Eve, transgression and childbearing. It does not settle the interpretation of saved through childbearing or adjudicate gender roles.
The source names the woman Life in Genesis 3:20 and Eve in Genesis 4:1. Both labels are retained rather than silently standardized.
No claim is made that the skin garments establish a sacrifice, blood atonement or a particular typology; the retained links concern actual clothing and divine provision.

The supplied text concerns offering rightly and dividing rightly, then says Be still. His turning shall be toward you, and you shall rule over him. Familiar sin crouching wording is not imported. The final pronoun reference and the full ritual interpretation remain unadjudicated; retained parallels concern worship and conduct only.

The supplied edition reads My guilt is too great for me to be forgiven. Cross-references contrast that wording with forgiveness texts; they do not replace it with an alternate punishment-too-great reading or infer a settled psychological diagnosis.

The Cain-line Enoch, Methuselah and Lamech must not be merged with names in Seth's line. Genesis 4:18 retains Gaidad, Maiel and Methuselah exactly as supplied. Genealogical cross-references are labelled contrasts, not identical-person matches.
Comparison with the one-flesh text identifies a narrative difference between Lamech's two wives and the earlier pair. It does not invent an explicit divine judgment at Genesis 4:19.

The Exodus range is limited to corresponding bodily injuries. Its surrounding Greek-based fetal-formation case at Exodus 21:22-23 was read; this review does not restate it as an unrelated universal legal rule or adjudicate its disputed implications.
The source reads He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God. The record does not replace this with a different edition's statement about people first beginning worship.

Chronological correspondence pairs check only the arithmetic of the supplied Genesis ages. They do not harmonize those ages with another biblical edition or claim that Chronicles or Luke supplies matching ages.

Chronicles names Kenan where the supplied Genesis and Luke records use Cainan. The retained link is their corresponding position between Enosh and Mahalalel in the ancestry, with the English-name difference stated explicitly.

The supplied Enoch chronology is 165 years before Methuselah plus 200 afterward, totaling 365. Preserve that reading. Wisdom 4:10-14 does not name Enoch and is retained only as an approval-and-transfer thematic parallel.

The supplied Methuselah figures are 167 plus 802, totaling 969; Lamech is 188 plus 565, totaling 753. These exact source readings are not silently replaced by figures from another edition. This Seth-line Lamech is not equated with Cain-line Lamech in Genesis 4.
Marriage and offspring links retain the source language without resolving the disputed identity of the sons of God. No proposed angelic, Sethite or royal identification is counted as established.
The hundred and twenty years remain uninterpreted as to lifespan limit versus a period before judgment. The Peter patience link does not decide that question.
The supplied English says God took to heart and pondered. The rationale does not substitute the wording repented or regretted from a different textual stream.
Hebrews recalls ark preparation but does not repeat its measurements or roof specification. Those limits are stated in the relevant rationales; the tapering roof is not silently called a window.

The general pair instructions and later clean-creature sevens remain distinct. The retained fulfilment links quote the actual entrance passages rather than claiming that every later animal detail says only two.

The comprehensive obedience formula is a literary parallel in divine construction instructions. The two structures are not identified. The supplied Exodus context has no separate 40:7 or 40:11 units; neither missing unit is used as a target.

The supplied edition dates the opening flood, ark rest and final drying on the twenty-seventh day, rather than silently importing other editions' seventeenth-day readings. No reconstructed day-count calendar is asserted.

The supplied text says waters diminished until the tenth month and mountain tops appeared in the eleventh month. Both statements are preserved; no harmonization or independent textual-critical resolution is claimed.
The Genesis 1:2 comparison concerns divine action over waters before habitable ground appears. It does not identify wind and Spirit as identical or claim new original-language verification.
Clean-creature and burnt-offering comparisons with Leviticus are labelled thematic. They do not claim Noah had been given the later Sinai legislation.
The source's multiplication command is addressed to Noah at the release of creatures. It is not rewritten as an unambiguous command spoken directly to the animals.
The Acts food/blood comparison cites the actual apostolic letter at Acts 15:28-29 after reading the decision context, rather than attributing James' earlier proposal to a completed letter.
Actual target reading corrected the candidate numbering: in this Greek-based Exodus, 20:13 prohibits adultery, 20:14 theft, and 20:15 murder. The retained murder comparison uses 20:15.

Noah's creature-wide covenant, Abraham's covenant and Israel's Sabbath sign are compared as covenant forms; their audiences and provisions are not conflated. Ezekiel's rainbow is a shared image, not a restatement of Noah's covenant.

The review adds no unreported sexual act to Ham's behavior. The curse names Canaan; it is not transferred to all Ham's descendants or racial groups. Joshua 9:23 is a limited curse-and-servitude parallel.
The supplied pronoun in the dwelling clause is retained. The comparisons do not resolve whether its subject is God or Japheth.
